items.value: Waste-to-energy technologies
items.reasoning: Pyrolysis is the thermal decomposition of organic matter in the absence of oxygen, yielding syngas, bio-oil and char, and plasma gasification uses a plasma torch at very high temperature to break waste down into syngas and an inert slag. Both are thermochemical routes for converting municipal solid waste and other residues into energy, and neither belongs to rare-earth extraction, natural gas production or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles.

items.value: Neyyar, Peppara and Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries together with the Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
items.reasoning: The Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve straddles the southernmost Western Ghats across Kerala and Tamil Nadu and comprises Neyyar, Peppara and Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries with the adjoining Achankovil forests on the Kerala side, and the Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve on the Tamil Nadu side. The other option sets belong elsewhere: Mudumalai and Silent Valley to the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, and the Kaundinya, Papikonda, Kawal and Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam areas to the Eastern Ghats and Deccan.

items.value: All four are correct
items.reasoning: The adult green sea turtle grazes on seagrass and algae, so some turtles are herbivores. Parrotfish, surgeonfish and grass carp graze on algae and plants, so some fish are herbivores. The sirenians, dugongs and manatees, are marine mammals that feed on seagrass, so statement 3 holds. And many snakes, including sea snakes, boas and most vipers, give birth to live young rather than laying eggs, so statement 4 holds as well.

items.value: Pairs 1 and 3 only — the Irrawaddy dolphin is not a Chambal animal
items.reasoning: Pair 2 is decisively wrong: the Irrawaddy dolphin in India lives in the brackish Chilika Lake and adjoining coastal waters, while the dolphin of the Chambal is the Gangetic river dolphin. Since every other option keeps pair 2, the answer must be C on that ground alone. The remaining pairs also hold: the blue-finned mahseer occurs in the Deccan and Western Ghats drainages including the Cauvery, and the rusty-spotted cat, the world's smallest wild cat, is recorded from the Eastern Ghats besides central and western India.

items.value: Because they are harmful to marine ecosystems
items.reasoning: Microbeads are tiny solid plastic particles, usually under five millimetres, added to face scrubs, toothpastes and cleansers. They pass straight through sewage treatment into rivers and the sea, where they are eaten by plankton, fish and shellfish, accumulate along the food chain and adsorb persistent organic pollutants onto their surfaces. The concern is this marine and aquatic damage, not skin cancer, uptake by crops or food adulteration.

items.value: A sustainable source of textile fibre
items.reasoning: Girardinia diversifolia, the Himalayan or giant nettle known as allo, yields a long, strong bast fibre from its stem that is traditionally spun and woven in the central and eastern Himalaya, in Uttarakhand and Nepal, into bags, shawls and fabric. It has drawn attention as a wild, renewable, low-input textile fibre supporting hill livelihoods, rather than as a drug, biodiesel or paper-pulp source.

items.value: All three can be measured or estimated from satellite and remote-sensing data
items.reasoning: Chlorophyll content is retrieved from reflectance in the red and near-infrared through vegetation indices and hyperspectral methods, and land surface temperature is measured directly from thermal infrared sensors on satellites such as MODIS and Landsat, so 1 and 3 are certain. Statement 2 also holds: greenhouse gas emissions from paddies are estimated by combining satellite mapping of flooded rice extent and cropping calendars with emission models, and atmospheric methane over a region is itself sensed by instruments such as GOSAT and TROPOMI. Note also that no option offers 1 and 3 without 2, so the two certain statements together already force this answer.

items.value: Maharashtra, then Madhya Pradesh, then Odisha, then Chhattisgarh — that is 3-2-4-1
items.reasoning: Measured as forest cover as a share of the state's geographical area, Maharashtra is lowest at roughly 16.5 per cent, Madhya Pradesh next at about 25 per cent, Odisha higher at about 33 per cent, and Chhattisgarh highest at about 41 per cent. Ascending order is therefore Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, which is 3-2-4-1. Madhya Pradesh leads in absolute forest AREA, but its very large geographical area pushes its percentage well below Chhattisgarh's and Odisha's, which is the trap in this item.

items.value: All three statements about methane hydrate are correct
items.reasoning: Methane hydrate is an ice-like solid in which methane is caged in water molecules, stable only at low temperature and high pressure, so warming can destabilise it and release the gas, which is statement 1. Its two great reservoirs are exactly those named in statement 2, permafrost beneath the Arctic tundra and sediments beneath the continental-margin seafloor. Statement 3 is also right: methane has an atmospheric lifetime of roughly nine to twelve years, being removed chiefly by reaction with the hydroxyl radical and ending as carbon dioxide and water.

items.value: All four — carbon monoxide, methane, ozone and sulphur dioxide
items.reasoning: Incomplete combustion of crop residue emits carbon monoxide and methane directly, and the sulphur present in plant material is emitted as sulphur dioxide, so statements 1, 2 and 4 are certain. Ozone is not emitted directly but is formed in the atmosphere when the oxides of nitrogen and volatile organic compounds released by the burning react in sunlight, and biomass burning is a well-documented driver of raised tropospheric ozone. The structure of the options settles it too: no option offers 1, 2 and 4 without ozone, while A, B and C each drop one of the three species that are certainly emitted.

items.value: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 only — Croatia is on the Adriatic and Syria on the Mediterranean
items.reasoning: Albania's western coast faces the Adriatic, Kazakhstan has a long Caspian shoreline, and Morocco's northern coast on the Strait of Gibraltar is Mediterranean, so pairs 1, 3 and 4 hold. Pair 2 fails because Croatia lies on the Adriatic, the Black Sea being bordered by Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia, Georgia and Turkey. Pair 5 fails because Syria's coast is on the Mediterranean; the Red Sea is bordered by Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Jordan and Israel.

items.value: India
items.reasoning: India has been the world's largest exporter of rice by volume since the early 2010s, shipping well over ten million tonnes a year, driven by basmati to West Asia and non-basmati to Africa and neighbouring countries. Thailand and Vietnam follow, China is a net importer of rice despite being the largest producer, and Myanmar's exports are an order of magnitude smaller.

items.value: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 — Bandarpunch with the Yamuna, Bara Shigri with the Chenab, Siachen with the Nubra
items.reasoning: The Yamuna rises from the Yamunotri glacier on the flank of the Bandarpunch massif in Uttarakhand; the Bara Shigri glacier in Lahaul feeds the Chandra, which joins the Bhaga to form the Chandrabhaga or Chenab; and the Nubra river issues from the Siachen glacier in the Karakoram. Pair 3 is wrong because the Milam glacier in Pithoragarh feeds the Gori Ganga, the Mandakini rising instead from the Chorabari glacier above Kedarnath. Pair 5 is wrong because the Zemu glacier on Kanchenjunga feeds the Teesta, not the Manas.

items.value: They are pesticides used in agriculture
items.reasoning: Carbofuran is a carbamate while methyl parathion, phorate and triazophos are organophosphates; all four are highly toxic insecticides and acaricides applied to crops, and all four act by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase. Their acute toxicity to farm workers, birds and pollinators, and their residues on produce, are why their continued use in India is viewed with apprehension and why several have been recommended for a ban. They are not food preservatives, ripening agents or cosmetic ingredients.

items.value: Statement 3 only — the 2010 Rules extend to the drainage or catchment area of a wetland
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: the Ramsar Convention requires a party to designate at least one wetland for the List of Wetlands of International Importance and to promote the wise use of wetlands generally, but it does not oblige India to protect and conserve every wetland in its territory. Statement 3 is correct, since the 2010 Rules expressly bring within the definition of a wetland its zone of direct influence, that is the drainage area or catchment region as determined by the authority. Statement 2 is the doubtful one: the Rules were framed in exercise of powers under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and the Ramsar Convention does not issue recommendations directing member states to make such rules. RUNNER-UP: B, that is 2 and 3. B would win if the examiner treats the Rules as having been made to give effect to India's obligations as a Ramsar party, which is how they are often described; the whole item turns on statement 2 alone, since statement 1 is clearly false and statement 3 clearly true.

items.value: All three are correct
items.reasoning: Nitrogen fertiliser applied to fields is transformed by soil nitrification and denitrification, releasing nitrous oxide and nitric oxide to the air, so statement 1 holds. Cattle urine and dung release large quantities of ammonia through the breakdown of urea, making livestock the dominant source of atmospheric ammonia, so statement 2 holds. Poultry litter likewise volatilises ammonia and other reactive nitrogen compounds, so statement 3 holds. All three are standard components of the reactive nitrogen budget from agriculture.

items.value: All three are water reservoirs
items.reasoning: Aliyar is a dam and reservoir in the Anaimalai foothills of Coimbatore district in Tamil Nadu, Isapur is a large dam on the Penganga river in Nanded district of Maharashtra under the Upper Penganga project, and Kangsabati is a reservoir in Bankura and Purulia districts of West Bengal formed by damming the Kangsabati and Kumari rivers. What they share is that each is an artificial water reservoir; none is a uranium field, rainforest or cave system.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 only — H-CNG cuts carbon dioxide and hydrocarbon emissions, and up to about a fifth by volume can be hydrogen
items.reasoning: Blending hydrogen into compressed natural gas lowers the carbon content per unit of energy and improves combustion, so carbon dioxide and unburnt hydrocarbon emissions fall, which is statement 2. The accepted blend for bus fleets is about eighteen to twenty per cent hydrogen by volume, that is up to roughly one-fifth, which is statement 3. Statement 1 overstates the case: carbon monoxide is reduced but cannot be eliminated, because the methane in the blend still contains carbon. Statement 4 is wrong the other way, since producing and blending hydrogen adds cost, making H-CNG dearer than plain CNG.

items.value: Because clouds send the Earth's outgoing radiation back to the surface, so it does not cool to the dew point
items.reasoning: Dew forms when the ground loses heat by radiation on a clear, still night until its surface falls below the dew point and moisture condenses on it. A cloud cover returns the terrestrial radiation to the surface, so the ground stays warm, never reaches the dew point, and no dew forms. C is the opposite of the truth, since cloudy nights are warmer at the surface, and D describes nothing relevant. A names only absorption, which by itself would still let the surface lose heat and cool; it is the return of that energy to the ground that prevents dew. Strictly, clouds absorb and re-emit longwave radiation downwards rather than reflecting it, so the option's wording is loose, but B is the only choice that gives the correct causal explanation.

items.value: Statement 2 only — the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment
items.reasoning: Statement 1 inverts the history. It was the 39th Amendment of 1975 that inserted Article 329A placing the election of the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond judicial scrutiny; the 44th Amendment of 1978 did the opposite, repealing that provision and restoring judicial review. Statement 2 is correct: in the National Judicial Appointments Commission case of 2015 the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment and the accompanying NJAC Act as violating the independence of the judiciary, a basic feature of the Constitution, and revived the collegium system.

items.value: Statements 3 and 4 only
items.reasoning: Statement 3 is correct, since the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 lays down the procedure for investigating and proving misbehaviour or incapacity, including the three-member inquiry committee. Statement 4 is correct and reproduces Article 124(4): the address must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. Statement 1 is wrong because Section 3 of the same Act expressly allows the Speaker or the Chairman to admit the motion or to refuse to admit it. Statement 2 is wrong because the Constitution uses the expressions incapacity and proved misbehaviour without anywhere defining them.

items.value: Jawaharlal Nehru
items.reasoning: The Ninth Schedule was added by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, together with Article 31B, to shield the zamindari abolition and other land reform laws from challenge in the courts on the ground of violating fundamental rights. Nehru was Prime Minister and the amendment was moved by his government in the Provisional Parliament.

items.value: Statement 1 only — coal was nationalised under Indira Gandhi
items.reasoning: Coal nationalisation was carried out in two stages under Indira Gandhi, by the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act of 1972 and the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act of 1973, leading to the formation of Coal India Limited, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: after the cancellation of earlier allocations, the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 put blocks up for allocation by competitive auction, with allotment to public sector undertakings, and never by lottery. Statement 3 is wrong because India remains a large importer of coal, particularly coking coal for steel, and is not self-sufficient.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 only — the 1959 Act exempts several offices, and the Constitution does not define office of profit
items.reasoning: Statement 3 is plainly wrong: Articles 102 and 191 disqualify a member for holding an office of profit under the Government but nowhere define the expression, which is why its meaning has had to be worked out by the courts through tests of appointment, remuneration and control. Since every other option retains statement 3, A is the only possible answer, and the precise number of amendments in statement 2 does not have to be settled to reach it. Statement 1 is in any case correct, the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 listing offices whose holders are exempted from that disqualification.

items.value: The Fifth Schedule
items.reasoning: The Fifth Schedule governs the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes outside the north-east, and it empowers the Governor to make regulations that prohibit or restrict the transfer of land by or among members of Scheduled Tribes in those areas, on which basis such transfers, including transfers to private mining parties, can be held null and void. This was the reasoning of the Supreme Court in the Samatha case of 1997. The Third Schedule holds forms of oath, the Ninth Schedule the laws immune from fundamental-rights challenge, and the Twelfth Schedule the subjects of municipalities.
